newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA problems not seen widespread.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA problems not seen widespread.

text.p: Shares of Columbia/HCA slumped Friday on uncertainty surrounding a federal probe of its El Paso operations, but analysts said they did not expect any system-wide problems at the company.
"This is a squeaky clean company -- if there is a bad egg in the basket, Columbia will throw it against the wall," said Todd Richter of Dean Witter.
Peter Costa, an analyst with Chicago Corp, said: "The news is not being perceived well. We don't know what (federal investigators) are looking at."
But Costa also said he did not believe that El Paso's problems were company-wide.
Columbia stock lost 2-3/4, trading at 38-3/4 in the afternoon, an extension of Thursday's 1-1/8 point drop.

Late Wednesday, Columbia said that its El Paso, Texas operations had been served with search warrants related to a federal investigations. Columbia said it has not been informed of the allegations underlying the probe.

In a research report, A.J. Rice and Tom Gallucci from Bear Stearns noted that Columbia has previously been the subject of government investigations and that none have resulted in an adverse finding against the company.
Still, a cloud could remain over Columbia/HCA stock for a while. Costa noted that the Medicare investigation will take time.
"It will take a year or so for this to clear," he said.
